_meta.indication: Treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension (WHO Group 1) in patients with WHO class II or III symptoms to improve exercise capacity and delay clinical worsening

pivotal_trials.design: 12-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter study comparing once-daily 5 mg and 10 mg LETAIRIS to placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with PAH (WHO Group 1) with WHO functional class II-III symptoms
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in 6-minute walk distance at 12 weeks
pivotal_trials.result: Placebo-adjusted mean change in 6MWD of 31 m (5 mg, p=0.008) and 51 m (10 mg, p<0.001)

pivotal_trials.design: 12-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter study comparing once-daily 2.5 mg and 5 mg LETAIRIS to placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with PAH (WHO Group 1) with WHO functional class II-III symptoms
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in 6-minute walk distance at 12 weeks
pivotal_trials.result: Placebo-adjusted mean change in 6MWD of 32 m (2.5 mg, p=0.022) and 59 m (5 mg, p<0.001)

key_safety: Most common placebo-adjusted adverse reactions were peripheral edema (17% vs 11%), nasal congestion (6% vs 2%), sinusitis, flushing, palpitations, abdominal pain, and constipation; serious risks include potential liver injury (aminotransferase elevations) and decreases in hemoglobin
target_moa: High-affinity, highly ET_A-selective endothelin receptor antagonist that blocks ET_A-mediated vasoconstriction and cell proliferation in PAH

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for potential liver injury (aminotransferase elevations; monitor monthly) and contraindication in pregnancy (may cause fetal harm)

rems.type: Available only through a special restricted distribution program (RiskMAP) called the LETAIRIS Education and Access Program (LEAP), with mandatory liver function and pregnancy testing, due to risks of liver injury and birth defects

description.text: Added indication for use in combination with tadalafil to reduce the risks of disease progression and hospitalization for worsening PAH and to improve exercise ability, based on the AMBITION study

citations.quote: - In combination with tadalafil to reduce the risks of disease progression and hospitalization for worsening PAH, and to improve exercise ability.

orphan_indication.text: Treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH); orphan designation granted July 16, 2004 (Designation Request #04-1836)

citations.quote: The Food and Drug Administration's Office of Orphan Products Development designated ambrisentan for the treatment of PAH on July 16, 2004 (Designation Request #04-1836).

basis.text: The application was classified as a priority review

citations.quote: The application has been classified as a priority review.

summary.text: LETAIRIS was granted orphan drug designation for PAH and received a priority review. It was not an accelerated approval; it was approved with restrictions to assure safe use under the Subpart H restricted-distribution provisions (21 CFR 314.520), implemented through the RiskMAP/LEAP restricted distribution program.

citations.quote: The Food and Drug Administration's Office of Orphan Products Development designated ambrisentan for the treatment of PAH on July 16, 2004 (Designation Request #04-1836).
The application has been classified as a priority review.

It is approved with restrictions to assure safe use under the provisions of the Subpart H regulations (21 CFR 314.520), effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed labeling text, Medication Guide, RiskMAP, and carton and container labels.

requirement.text: Conduct a study examining the effects of LETAIRIS on 6-minute walk distance at peak and trough plasma concentrations, with study design agreed with the Division

citations.quote: 1. Gilead agrees to conduct a study examining the effects of LETAIRIS on 6-minute walk distance at peak and trough plasma concentrations, and further agrees to reach agreement on an appropriate study design with the Division.

requirement.text: Submit the results of the completed Phase 1 ketoconazole drug interaction study

citations.quote: 2. Gilead agrees to submit the results of the Phase 1 ketoconazole drug interaction study that has already been completed.

requirement.text: Explore the interaction potential of strong CYP2C19 inhibitors (e.g., omeprazole), cyclosporine A (OATP and P-gp inhibitor), and rifampin on ambrisentan pharmacokinetics in humans

citations.quote: 3. Gilead agrees to a post-approval commitment to explore the interaction potential of strong inhibitors of CYP2C19 (e.g. omeprazole) on ambresitant pharmacokinetics in humans. Gilead further agrees to explore the interaction potential of cyclosporine A (strong inhibitor of OATP and P-gp) and rifampin (inhibitor of OATP and inducer of P-gp, CYPs 3A and 2C19) on ambresitant pharmacokinetics in humans.
